subject: Error in hclust: bruvo.boot() poppr v 2.6.1

messages.author: f8ffd364f28b2f8c
messages.subject: Error in hclust: bruvo.boot() poppr v 2.6.1
parts:
Greetings,

I have SSR data set with hybrid individuals of varying ploidy (2-12). As such, I have been using the bruvo.boot() function to try and compare the data. The data set consists of a set of SSR markers that have a 3 nucleotide motif however alleles have been observed within the set that differ by less than 3 nucleotides. Additionally, some of the alleles are true null alleles and have been coded as zeros. When running the data set with the individuals with null alleles I receive the following error:

Error in hclust(DD, method = method, ...) : 
  NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 11)

If I remove the individuals that are null at these markers the function runs fine and no error is produced.

Is there a recommended way to code these individuals to handle the possibility of null alleles?

My initial thought is to code the allele as either 001 or 999. For example, a tetraploid individual with a null allele the coding would be 001/001/001/001 or 999/999/999/999

Is this an appropriate way to treat the problem?

Jason

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Error in hclust: bruvo.boot() poppr v 2.6.1
parts:
Hello,

The error is coming from the presence of missing data in your distance matrix due to randomly sampling entirely null alleles for an individual. In cases like this, use the ape function "njs" as the tree parameter. 

Regarding null alleles, yes, coding them as 999 or 001 should give you the effect that the distance for individuals with null alleles will be 1 at that locus. However, this is a bit of a hack since these alleles do not fit within the stepwise mutation framework and the result would be increased genetic distances at these individuals, so you will want to check for clustering by the presence of null alleles. 

Hope that helps,
Zhian
